facts.text: The Australian magpie can mimic more than 35 species of native and introduced birds, as well as dogs and horses.
facts.quote: the bird can mimic over 35 species of native and introduced bird species, as well as dogs and horses.

facts.text: Magpies can recognise at least 100 different people and may spare those they have befriended when swooping.
facts.quote: Research has shown that magpies can recognise at least 100 different people, and may be less likely to swoop individuals they have befriended.

facts.text: It has learned to eat poisonous cane toads safely by flipping them over and eating the underparts.
facts.quote: It has even learnt to safely eat the poisonous cane toad by flipping it over and consuming the underparts.

facts.text: Before swallowing prey, magpies rub off bee stingers and the irritating hairs of caterpillars.
facts.quote: Smaller prey are swallowed whole, although magpies rub off the stingers of bees, stinging ants and wasps and irritating hairs of caterpillars before swallowing.

facts.text: Chicks hatch around 20 days after incubation begins, pink, naked and blind with a bright red throat.
facts.quote: The chicks hatch synchronously around 20 days after incubation begins; like all passerines, the chicks are altricial—they are born pink, naked, and blind with large feet, a short broad beak and a bright red throat.

facts.text: A small minority of breeding magpies, almost always males, swoop at people who approach their nests.
facts.quote: a small minority of breeding magpies (almost always males) become aggressive, swooping and attacking those who approach their nests.

facts.text: Pairs of magpies sing a loud musical duet called carolling to advertise or defend their territory.
facts.quote: Pairs of magpies often take up a loud musical calling known as carolling to advertise or defend their territory

facts.text: The female builds the nest alone, usually high up in a tree fork and often in an exposed position.
facts.quote: Nests are built exclusively by females and generally placed high up in a tree fork, often in an exposed position.

facts.text: Australian magpies generally live to around 25 years of age, with some recorded reaching 30 years.
facts.quote: Australian magpies generally live to around 25 years of age, though ages of up to 30 years have been recorded.

facts.text: Helper birds sometimes assist magpie pairs in feeding and raising their young, a practice known as cooperative breeding.
facts.quote: The Australian magpie is known to engage in cooperative breeding, and helper birds will assist in feeding and raising young.
